structured.answer: I'm not deciding anything. Government bonds ("אג"ח ממשלתית צמודה") and "מק"מ" sound as safe as my deposit, so I'll ask my son or the bank about them. The page gives no numbers, so I can't tell whether they pay more or what the bank takes from me.

stuck.why: The scroll skipped past the deposit and savings-plan boxes. I only saw the ends, 'ריבית' and 'מוסכמת בריבית', and never read what it says about my own deposit
One says you buy for less than you get back at the end, the other says 'בלי ריבית ובלי הצמדה'. I couldn't tell whether there is interest or not
It's called a 'קרן נאמנות', the kind that fell on me before, but it also says 'סיכון נמוך'. I didn't know which to believe
English letters and מדד used to mean shares. I stopped reading there

used: Opening section 'שני חלקים בכל חיסכון' (פיקדון, אג"ח)
אג"ח ממשלתית צמודה box ('צמודות למדד המחירים לצרכן')
Footer 'אתר אישי, לא מסחרי, בלי קישורי שיווק'
skimmed: קרן השתלמות and קופת גמל להשקעה
skipped: קופת גמל / קרן השתלמות בניהול אישי
All the מדד boxes (S&P 500, MSCI World, MSCI AC World, נאסד"ק 100, ת"א-35/90/125)
not_found: Any interest rates or numbers comparing these with a bank deposit
Anything on bank fees, or whether the bank takes too much
The text of the פיקדון and תכנית חיסכון boxes (they scrolled past)

findings.what: No numbers at all, so there's no way to see whether anything pays more than a deposit
Fees or the bank's charges are never mentioned
The deposit and savings-plan boxes, the ones most relevant to me, went past on the scroll and I couldn't read them
findings.where: Bottom of screen 1 / top of screen 2

findings.what: מק"מ is described twice and the two seem to contradict each other about interest
'מדד' is used for share indexes, and most boxes at the end are English share-index names
Unknown site name 'מקור', not a bank, so it's hard to trust
Small grey subtitles and footer text are hard to read; the white-on-black screen tires the eyes
קרן כספית is called a קרן נאמנות and also low risk, which is confusing for someone burned by a fund
Screens 4 and 5 are almost the same
